description: An arriving command envelope plus the target's own state to an accept-or-refuse decision with exactly one enumerated reason. Authenticity, freshness, future-dating, replay, and permission are one composed decision rather than three independent checks a caller assembles, because the composition is the security property: a caller that checks authenticity and forgets replay has a working system with a silent hole. Several reasons can hold at once, so the check order is part of the contract and is pinned by the precedence cases below: authenticityUnverified, then replayedNonce, then futureDated, then stale, then notPermitted. Authenticity is first because every reason after it leaks something about the target's state, so nothing may precede it. The freshness window is 120 seconds and the future tolerance is 30 seconds; both boundaries are inclusive-accept.

cases.description: The ordinary accepted case: a signed, fresh, unseen command from a paired device with remote control on. It creates a job on the target; it does not power anything off here, and the remote countdown still applies.

Keep-awake is remotely permitted on the same terms as power-off, and likewise reaches the device as a job. One accepted case per remotely-permitted command, so a rule that accepted only power-off would fail here.
Cancelling remotely is permitted and goes through the target's existing job-cancellation path. The third and last remotely-permitted command.

Everything else is in order and only the signature failed to verify. The rule takes the verification outcome as an input rather than performing cryptography, so this is the single field that distinguishes a genuine command from a forged one.

Authentic, fresh, and permitted, but the target has already acted on this nonce. Freshness alone does not prevent replay: a command captured and resent immediately is still fresh, so both rules are required and neither substitutes for the other.

Dated well beyond the future tolerance, with nothing else wrong. Reported distinctly from staleness: a sender clock running ahead and a command that sat too long are different faults, and a user shown 'expired' for a clock-skew problem looks in the wrong place.
Authentic, unseen, and permitted, but issued well outside the freshness window. A captured command must not stay obeyable forever, and a power-off cannot be undone.

Authentic, fresh, and unseen, but the target's owner has not turned remote control on. Permission is delegated to the existing authorization rule, which keeps its own reason set; acceptance reports only that the command was not permitted.

An authentic, fresh command from a device that is not paired with this target. Pairing is the only act that confers authority, so an unpaired sender is refused on permission grounds even though its signature verified.

An age of exactly 120 seconds is accepted. The boundary is inclusive-accept by decision rather than by whichever comparison operator an implementation happens to use, which is why it is pinned here and paired with the case one second past.
121 seconds old, one second past the window, and refused. The other half of the freshness boundary: without both, an implementation using the wrong comparison passes.

Dated exactly 30 seconds ahead and accepted. Ordinary clock skew between two honest devices must not refuse a valid command, and this boundary is inclusive-accept for the same reason the freshness one is.

Dated 31 seconds ahead and refused as futureDated, not as stale. Every second of tolerance is a second added to the window in which a captured command stays obeyable, so the tolerance is small on purpose.

The same nonce arriving a second time within the freshness window, among several the target has already seen. This is the case the nonce store exists for, and it must be refused for as long as the freshness window would otherwise let the command through.

A second command from the same paired device bearing a different nonce is accepted. Without this case an implementation could refuse every command from a device that had ever sent one and still pass the replay cases.

Two reasons hold: the signature did not verify and the nonce has been seen. Authenticity surfaces, so an unauthenticated caller cannot learn which nonces the target has already acted on by replaying captured ones.

Two reasons hold: the signature did not verify and remote control is off. Authenticity surfaces, which is the spec's no-probing requirement: a caller must not be able to read the target's permission state out of refusals to unauthenticated commands.

Two reasons hold: the nonce has been seen and the command is dated beyond tolerance. Replay surfaces, because a replayed command is evidence of an attack whereas a skewed clock is usually an honest fault, and the record should show an attack as an attack.
Two reasons hold: the nonce has been seen and the command is long past the freshness window. Replay surfaces for the same reason — a stale command is more often a bad network, a replayed one is not.

A command cannot be both future-dated and stale — the two are mutually exclusive by construction — so the case that pins futureDated's place in the order sets it against notPermitted. Dated beyond tolerance with remote control off: futureDated surfaces, and permission, which discloses the most, is not reached.

Two reasons hold: the command is stale and it is not permitted. Staleness surfaces. notPermitted is checked last because it leaks the most — whether remote control is enabled and what the platform can do — and is reached only by a command already authentic, fresh, and new.

Every reason holds: the signature failed, the nonce has been seen, the command is dated beyond tolerance, and it would not be permitted. The first in the order wins, so the refusal discloses nothing beyond the authenticity failure. An unordered implementation would return any of several answers here and fail intermittently.

Authentic, fresh, and unseen, but enabling remote control is not a command any target accepts remotely. Requiring physical presence to grant the permission is what keeps account access alone from being enough to power off every device on it.
